result.markdown: --- title: "[vals.fmt_roman()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-function}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Format values as Roman numerals. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/posit-dev/great-tables/blob/main/great_tables/_formats_vals.py#L1122-L1169){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python vals.fmt_roman(x, case="upper", pattern="{x}") ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} With numeric values we can transform those to Roman numerals, rounding values as necessary. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [x]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [X]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A list of values to be formatted. [case]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["upper"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Should Roman numerals should be rendered as uppercase (`"upper"`) or lowercase (`"lower"`) letters? By default, this is set to `"upper"`. [pattern]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["{x}"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : A formatting pattern that allows for decoration of the formatted value. The formatted value is represented by the `{x}` (which can be used multiple times, if needed) and all other characters will be interpreted as string literals. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A list of formatted values is returned. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#114ab552 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} from great_tables import vals vals.fmt_roman([3, 5]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ['III', 'V'] ``` ::: :::
